svg.title: Johan S. Varughese. I study when machine learning can be trusted.
svg.text: I study when machine learning can be trusted.

text.tspan: Abstract.
A model can be accurate and still not deserve trust. My work asks
four narrower questions: whether a federated model leaks what it promised to
hide, whether a training run was the run it claims to be, whether an LLM
judge’s biases compound, and whether an interpretability tool still tells the
truth once the model is steered. I then test those ideas where the stakes are
clinical: HER2 breast-cancer scoring for Kerala’s government medical colleges.
I’m a final-year B.Tech student in CSE (AI) at Mar Baselios College of
Engineering and Technology, where I founded IRIS, the college’s first
undergraduate research lab.
Seven manuscripts so far, three at NeurIPS 2026
workshops.
BiomarkHER2, and the HER2 IHC track of
the LoFi/MedG project at Dr. Xiaoxiao Li’s
TEA Lab, UBC.
Founded 2026. Thirteen members; six or
seven more papers are in development by
other members.
Reviewer for ICMLA 2026 and the NeurIPS
2026 InterpScience workshop. MATS Winter
2027, stage 2.
